note.note:
Medical History

- Current health concerns and risk factors:  New severe continuous headache x3 days; diffuse, worse over right eye; photophobia; intermittent “shooting lights” visual disturbance; mild nausea without vomiting; severity 8/10 improving to ~5/10 with ibuprofen but not resolving; able to sleep, not waking from sleep; present on waking; brief stabbing pain when standing quickly; sensation of “something moving” with sudden head movement; no fever, URI/sinus symptoms, or focal neurologic deficits; on combined oral contraceptive; family history of migraine; alcohol weekly; non-smoker.  
- Relevant family medical history:  Mother with severe migraines (with vomiting). Otherwise not recorded.  
- Medications (including OTC or shared medications):  Combined oral contraceptive pill (brand not documented), started ~1 year ago; ibuprofen PRN for headache (dose/route/frequency not documented); new prescription for a stronger NSAID to use instead of ibuprofen (name/dose/route/frequency not documented); advised to take acetaminophen (paracetamol) concurrently. No known drug allergies.  
- Immunisation status reviewed:  Not recorded.  
- Sexual and reproductive health:  On combined oral contraceptive for contraception x1 year; no side effects noted; BP last checked at pharmacy 1 year ago and reported normal; clinician advised pill may need to change if migraine with aura confirmed.  
- Physical activity and nutrition:  Not recorded.  
- Alcohol, tobacco, and substance use:  Non-smoker; alcohol about once weekly (~3 drinks/session); no illicit drug use reported.  
- Hearing loss or concerns:  Not recorded.  
- Mood/mental health (including depression, self-harm risk):  Not recorded (reports difficulty focusing and reduced ability to work due to headache).  
- Vision problems or recent changes:  Recent optometry check reportedly normal; current photophobia and transient visual phenomena during headache; no persistent vision loss reported.  
- Family and social relationships, caring responsibilities:  Lives alone; works from home; work attendance/efficiency reduced over last 3 days due to headache. Caring responsibilities not recorded.  

Examination

- BP, pulse rate and rhythm:  Not recorded (to be checked at in-person visit).  
- Height, weight, BMI, waist circumference (if indicated):  Not recorded.  
- Oral exam (including dentition and gums):  Not recorded.  
- Ear exam (otoscopy, whisper test if needed):  Not recorded.  
- Vision/eye exam (basic screen):  Not recorded (fundoscopy planned at in-person visit).  
- Urinalysis (dipstick for proteinuria):  Not recorded.  

Investigations (as indicated)

- Fasting BGL and lipids (or random BGL if needed):  Not recorded.  
- Cervical screening (if eligible and due):  Not recorded.  
- STI screen (urine or swab – chlamydia/gonorrhoea if age 15–35):  Not recorded.  
- Mammogram (if eligible):  Not recorded.  
- Other pathology (e.g., HbA1c, iron studies, Vitamin D):  Not recorded.  

Assessment & Plan (Integrating DDx)

- Key findings: New, continuous severe headache x3 days with photophobia and positive visual phenomena; right supraorbital predominance; mild nausea; no focal neurologic symptoms; afebrile by history; partial relief with NSAID; family history of migraine; combined estrogen-containing OCP use.  
- Working diagnosis: Probable migraine with aura; persistent >72 hours raises possibility of status migrainosus.  
- Differential considerations consistent with DDx:  
  - Cerebral venous sinus thrombosis (CVST) needs consideration given new severe headache and estrogen OCP use, despite no focal deficits (moderate concern).  
  - Tension-type headache less likely given migrainous features and severity.  
- Management priorities: In-person assessment for full neurologic exam and fundoscopy; measure BP; trial stronger NSAID with acetaminophen; safety-net to emergency care if red flags develop or symptoms worsen; review contraceptive suitability if migraine with aura confirmed. No conflicts noted between transcript and DDx.

Management Plan

- Arrange in-person appointment via support team for:  
  - Full neurologic examination and fundoscopic exam.  
  - Blood pressure measurement.  
- Medications:  
  - Start prescribed stronger NSAID instead of ibuprofen; take with food (name/dose/route/frequency not documented).  
  - May take acetaminophen (paracetamol) concurrently as advised.  
- Safety-net:  
  - Go to emergency department if headache worsens, becomes unbearable, changes character, or if new symptoms occur (weakness, numbness, vision loss, persistent vomiting, fever, neck stiffness, seizures).  
- Contraception:  
  - If migraine with aura is confirmed, discuss changing from combined OCP to a safer alternative.  
- Follow-up:  
  - Proceed with the booked in-person review; may cancel if symptoms fully resolve before then per clinician advice.

- Allied health referral (EPC – 10 visits):  Not recorded.  
- Reproductive or sexual health clinic referral:  Not recorded.  
- Mental health support if indicated (e.g., psychologist, AMS support):  Not recorded.  
- CTG registration:  Not recorded.  
- Preventive health follow-up booked (e.g., flu vaccine, Pap test):  Not recorded.

Summary of Differential Diagnoses (from DDx)

- Migraine with aura (possible status migrainosus) – Likelihood: High  
  Justification: Severe headache with photophobia and positive visual phenomena; right peri-orbital emphasis; mild nausea; family history; partial NSAID response; persistent >72 hours.  
- Cerebral venous sinus thrombosis (CVST) – Likelihood: Moderate  
  Justification: New persistent severe headache in a woman on estrogen-containing OCP; visual symptoms; some positional sensitivity; absence of deficits does not exclude.  
- Tension-type headache – Likelihood: Low-Moderate  
  Justification: Constant diffuse pressure could fit; however, photophobia/visual phenomena and severity favor migraine.

Quality checks

- Missing expected elements: Vitals (BP, pulse), BMI/anthropometrics, urinalysis, neurological and fundoscopic exam, immunization review, comprehensive mental health screening, dental/oral health check, hearing assessment, preventive care review (cervical screening, STI screening, vaccinations), detailed medication doses/frequencies.  
- Internal contradictions: None noted between transcript and DDx.  
- Transcript quality: Some audio issues and redacted information (patient name and pill brand); overall history adequate for telehealth but lacks physical examination and objective measurements.
